A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and can be matched despite extensive reformatting and theorem renumbering.

before.justification: Section 7 and Figures 3–4 report original stochastic-gridworld experiments evaluating CVaR Q-learning, value iteration, safety outcomes, and discretization accuracy.

after.justification: v2 retains these original gridworld experiments and their results, with experimental details in Appendix D.

M1.justification: Section 5, footnote 4 newly suggests an optional adaptation: replace r(s,a) with r(s,a) − r_gamma to obtain non-positive rewards while preserving the optimal CVaR policy. The Bellman updates and Algorithms 1–4 otherwise retain their procedures; the experiments do not report using this adaptation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 4 × 5 stochastic Crater Walk environment and safe, fuel-efficient navigation task. No datasets, domains, or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Figure 3 retains the same comparisons between static CVaR Q-learning and Q-value iteration, including the risk-neutral policy in the CVaR comparison. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Appendix D.2 corrects the stated discretization interval from [−100 − ν, −100 + ν] to [−100 − ν, 100 + ν]. With ν = 10, this changes the documented range from [−110, −90] to [−110, 110], retaining 5,000 bins. This is a correction to a reported setting; it does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Figure 4 retains the same discretization sensitivity study using 100, 500, 1,000, and 5,000 bins. The risk-level analyses of return distributions, crater entries, and learning convergence are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report 10 independent seeds for each algorithm and retain identical plotted variability and discussion of higher variance near α = 0.5–0.6. No uncertainty-estimation procedure or statistical test is added.

E6.justification: Figures 3–4 contain identical empirical plots, and Section 7 retains the same performance, safety, convergence, and discretization findings. The corrected grid specification is not accompanied by revised results.

T1.justification: The new Section 5 footnote adds a mathematical argument invoking CVaR translation invariance to justify a policy-preserving reward shift. The existing theorem statements, bounds, and Appendix B proofs remain substantively unchanged after matching their new numbering.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: exact static-CVaR reformulation, dense rewards, contraction on bounded functions, discretized algorithms, and convergence and approximation guarantees.

C2.justification: The reward-translation footnote clarifies that the non-positive-reward assumption can be satisfied without changing the optimal CVaR policy. Interpretations of the empirical results and the limitation to tabular experiments remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link in the abstract and corrects the grid interval in Appendix D.2. Appendix D.4 also adds a promise to release implementations upon acceptance, leaving release-status wording inconsistent with the abstract. Actual repository availability cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning are retained. The anonymous Predictive CVaR Q-learning citation becomes Kim and Min (2026), and several preprints receive publication metadata; these are updates to the same works.

P1.justification: v2 makes grammatical corrections, rewrites the transition into discretization, adds a brief Impact Statement, and updates acknowledgments and affiliations. Citations become author–year and theorem numbering becomes section-based, while the narrative and section order remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from a single-column manuscript to a two-column conference layout, with new typography, running headers, and extensive reflow of equations, algorithms, and figures. Appendices are also retypeset. The same five figures and two tables remain, with resizing, relocation, and limited caption edits.

improvement.justification: Correcting the grid interval in Appendix D.2 removes a concrete reproducibility error, while the reward-translation explanation clarifies applicability and the abstract provides code-access information. These are limited, useful improvements; the empirical evidence and main proofs are unchanged. The inconsistent code-release wording limits what can be concluded about implementation availability.
